definitions.gloss: wind and rain; storm; stormy weather
definitions.explanation: Wind and rain occurring together, typically implying harsh or stormy conditions. A formal compound used in weather reports and news rather than casual conversation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{激|はげ}しい→激しい：02348_hageshii⟧{風雨|ふうう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いている→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
{風雨|ふうう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧さらされて⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧だいぶ⟦{傷|いた}んでいる→傷む：10061_itamu⟧。
examples.english: The building has deteriorated considerably from exposure to wind and rain.

examples.japanese: ⟦{台風|たいふう}→台風：01455_taifuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{伴|ともな}う→伴う：10389_tomonau⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧{風雨|ふうう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧、⟦{本日|ほんじつ}→本日：09643_honjitsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{屋外|おくがい}→屋外：04136_okugai⟧⟦イベント→イベント：09594_ibento⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{中止|ちゅうし}→中止：03481_chuushi⟧となりました。
examples.english: Due to strong wind and rain accompanying the typhoon, today's outdoor event has been cancelled.

notes:
A compound word referring to wind and rain together, typically implying stormy or harsh weather. Combines {風|ふう} (wind) and {雨|う} (rain).

USAGE:
- Used in weather reports, news, and formal descriptions of weather conditions
- Implies both wind and rain occurring simultaneously — not just one or the other
- Also used figuratively in the expression {風雨|ふうう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{耐|た}える→耐える：12087_taeru⟧ (to weather the storm), meaning to endure hardships
- More formal than simply saying ⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風雨|ふうう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{強|つよ}まる→強まる：02295_tsuyomaru⟧: wind and rain intensify
- {風雨|ふうう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧さらされる: to be exposed to wind and rain
- {風雨|ふうう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{耐|た}える→耐える：12087_taeru⟧: to withstand wind and rain; to weather the storm
- {暴|ぼう}{風雨|ふうう}: violent storm, tempest

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{暴風雨|ぼうふうう}→暴風雨：07670_boufuuu⟧: tempest, violent storm — a more intense version
- ⟦{荒天|こうてん}→荒天：16432_kouten⟧: stormy weather, bad weather — broader term for poor weather conditions
- ⟦{嵐|あらし}→嵐：01695_arashi⟧: storm — the everyday word, more dramatic
